summary: LUKS keyslot rotation fails after depot NVMe firmware update causing check-in and mounting errors
description:
Issue summary: Several devices returned from the depot with NVMe firmware applied. After reinstallation and Intune check-in, machines fail to complete LUKS keyslot rotation during first boot; resulting in intermittent mount failures and enrollment-agent retries.

Impact: Fleet devices repaired in depot may not become usable for engineers. Affected machines show blocked check-in and fail to mount user volume; blocks provisioning workflows and requires manual recovery. Estimated 8 devices reported in last 48 hours.

Environment: Production images deployed via depot repair workflow. Devices include Dell Latitude 7440 and Lenovo X1 Gen9. NVMe FW version reported 6C1.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Depot reimage and NVMe firmware flash (standard depot process)
2) Apply corporate WIM, boot to OOBE, device enrolls to Intune
3) Enrollment agent triggers LUKS keyslot rotation (post-provision step)
4) Keyslot rotation process errors with exit code 74 and kernel logs show cryptographic device I/O errors

Observed logs and errors:
- Enrollment agent logs: "luks-rotate: exit 74: failed to write keyslot metadata"
- dmesg: "nvme nvme0: I/O 0, completion timeout, status: 0x81" and later "blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 2048"
- systemd-journal: repeated journal entries for systemd-cryptsetup@luks-user.service failing to create new keyslot

Hypothesis: NVMe firmware update changes write path timing or power management characteristics that cause small metadata writes (keyslot headers) to fail under the current depot flash/firmware sequence. Alternatively, firmware sets a vendor-specific caching behavior that isn't flushed before LUKS operation.

Workaround (temporary): Manual recovery on affected device: boot live USB, dd backup of LUKS header, use cryptsetup luksAddKey with --key-file against existing mapped device, then run hdparm --flush-cache and ensure NVMe write cache is flushed before attempting keyslot rotation. Not scalable for depot volumes.

Desired resolution: Identify root cause (firmware setting vs image timing), implement depot flash/flush step or adjust post-repair provisioning to ensure safe keyslot operations, and roll out automated remediation for devices currently in the wild.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Priya Shah (Support): Ticket created after two reports from depot QA. Collected logs and serial numbers. Initial triage indicates NVMe I/O errors immediately preceding LUKS failures.
2026-03-10 - Depot Team (comment): Confirmed firmware 6C1 applied to 5 units yesterday in batch A. We used the new NVMe flasher from vendor v2.1. No errors on flashing step itself.

2026-03-11 - Ethan Morales (SRE): Reproduced locally in lab on Lenovo X1 with FW 6C1. Observed small write failures when keyslot write occurs within 3s of firmware reset. If we insert a 10s sleep+cache flush, rotation succeeds.

2026-03-11 - Storage Eng (comment): Filing upstream with NVMe vendor. Suspect controller doesn't honor cache flush on reset; requesting vendor errata. Opening GH issue at https://github.com/nvme-vendor/firmware-issues/issues/57
2026-03-12 - Ethan Morales (SRE): Added temporary depot script to run 'nvme flush' and sleep 12s after firmware flash. Deploying to two depots as pilot. Marking ticket In Progress.

2026-03-12 - Security (comment): Need confirmation this workaround retains FIPS-compliant behavior; also confirm LUKS header integrity checks post-fix. Security requests automated post-repair verification steps added to runbook.
investigation_notes: Lab reproduction successful. Key observations: failures occur when cryptsetup performs a small metadata write within ~5s of NVMe reset. Adding an explicit nvme flush and 12s delay prevents the error. Kernel logs show vendor-specific completion bits set on command completion that are inconsistent with write durability. Tentatively filing bug with NVMe vendor and coordinating depot automation change.
resolution: Mitigation applied: Depot scripting updated to run 'nvme flush' and sleep 12s after firmware flash in the repair workflow; pilot deployed to WA depot 1 and confirmed on 6 test devices. Long term: awaiting vendor firmware patch; plan to add automated LUKS header verification step in post-repair checklist and telemetry to detect similar failures. Security signed off on workaround pending vendor patch. Closure will follow vendor fix and rollout verification.
